answer: Each agent could be required to keep its own unique encrypted archive, a slab of data as dense as shale, sealed with a key only it holds. Verifiers send random spot checks, like a sudden plume of queries, asking for slices that must be returned within seconds. A sybil farm running a thousand identities needs a thousand distinct archives on real disks, so its storage bill climbs with every fake, and that opal-bright reward stops being worth the hardware.
